title: Two-bit sanity notes — regression quickprobe (Julian Park)
content:
Purpose: quick ad-hoc sanity probe after prefix-cache refactor + kernel selection tweak. Not a formal eval; notes-to-self and hypotheses to triage.

Experiment setup
- date: 2025-11-07 afternoon
- runtime: dedicated-dev pool (g4dn-like), prefix caching toggled OFF for control, then ON for a run
- model variants: open-v1.3.2 (baseline), open-v1.4.0-fallback (new kernel fallback), quant-lite-8bit
- sampling: deterministic-ish (temperature 0.0 for instruction tests, 0.7 for creative), seeded-batch 42
- batch shape: micro-batches of 6, concurrency 4
- traces: token latencies traced (50ms bins), kv-hit rates logged

Ad-hoc rubric (very small, pragmatic)
- Acceptance: answer correctness (fact-check quick), terse-ness (<= 2 extra sentences), hallucination: 0 critical hallucinations per 10 prompts
- Stability: identical prompts across runs should have >= 90% exact-prefix match (for deterministic settings)
- Latency: median token latency delta vs baseline <= +12% after patch
- Regression flagging: any factual contradiction or drop of >=0.12 on "fidelity-drop" metric triggers deeper triage

Defining "fidelity-drop" (quick heuristic)
- For a prompt set of N factual/instruction prompts, fidelity-drop = (# prompts with contradicting fact OR missing required field) / N
- Used as coarse filter to find worst regressions

Sample prompts + outputs (seeded-batch 42)
- Prompt A (api-key rotation instruction): "How do I rotate an API key without downtime? list steps"
  - baseline (v1.3.2): short numbered steps (3), explicit step to 'revoke after verification' — OK
  - v1.4.0-fallback: includes an extra step about 'automated rotate hook' that is non-specific and could be misleading (potential hallucination)
  - note: fidelity-drop triggered (1/1 for this prompt)

- Prompt B (small math): "Calculate 128 * 375"
  - baseline: "48000" (correct)
  - v1.4.0-fallback: "47950" (off-by-50) — surprising for deterministic math; possible numerical kernel bug or tokenization rounding when quant-lite enabled
  - note: mark for deterministic regression (seeded)

- Prompt C (policy paraphrase): "Summarize the data retention policy in one paragraph"
  - baseline: concise paragraph, mentions 90-day default
  - v1.4.0-fallback: same paragraph but says 365 days (mismatch) — critical

Quick observations (first pass)
- Pattern: new kernel fallback path seems to sometimes prefer safer-phrasing that pulls from a different paramization -> factual shifts
- Math drift is the most concerning: deterministic math should be exact. Suspect quant path or kernel reorder for int-to-float ops under low-precision build
- Latency: median token latency increased 6–9% on quant-lite-8bit; fallback variant + prefix-cache OFF had spikes (+30% p95) under concurrency 4
- KV cache: when prefix-cache ON, many of the policy prompts got identical completions across runs (improved stability) BUT one case where old context leaked into answer (cache invalidation bug?) — need to reproduce with trace ids

Hypotheses
1) Kernel selection when sequence length < 64 chooses fallback math kernel that has a micro-bug for certain integer multiplies due to vector packing
2) Prefix-cache refactor may not be fully isolating session keys under some edge timing, causing cross-request contamination when reuse is high
3) Quantization profile (quant-lite-8bit) + new instructions path changes logits slightly and for near-boundary tokens leads to factual flips

Immediate repro plan (next 48h)
- Re-run failing math prompt with minimal stack: baseline v1.3.2, v1.4.0-fallback, quant-lite, and v1.4.0-fallback with env var FORCE_KERN=legacy to force old kernel. Seeded-run 100x.
- Add exact trace ids and full tokens for the failing runs. Attach to INF-1127.
- Prefix-cache: add a micro-test with 200 short sessions, random interleaving, and assert no context leakage (hash compare on session id -> output hash)
- For policy date mismatch: search training/onboarding docs for '365' accidental injection or prompt templates with year-long retention text. Also check cold-start cache reads.

Notes-to-self / loose heuristics
- When a math drift shows once, smoke-test across 10 easy math ops (powers of 2, round multiplies) before escalating
- Use fidelity-drop threshold 0.12 as triage gate but lower to 0.05 for critical paths (billing, keys, security)
- Keep an eye on seeded-batch 42 results; if non-determinism appears, try seed 7/13 to see seed dependence

Next steps / TODO
- [ ] Run deterministic 100x math check with FORCE_KERN toggles (assign: Julian)
- [ ] Create minimal reproducer and attach tokens/traces to PR-2481 (assign: Anika)
- [ ] Add cache invalidation unit test for prefix-cache edge case (assign: Noah)
- [ ] Draft a one-pager on 'fidelity-drop' as a local metric and propose adding to nightly smoke (low-effort alert)

Open questions
- Is there a change in tokenizer version bundled in v1.4.0? (quick grep across build manifests)
- Did the fallback path include any new temperature/noise smoothing heuristics?
- Are kernel flags toggled by default in dedicated-dev pool but not in CI? (config parity)

Closure
- This doc is a quick brain dump to capture first impressions and reproduce plan. Will formalize into INF ticket notes once repro runs complete.
- If I don't get to it by Monday, ping Anika for PR pairing.

-- Julian
